title: KB Securities Prepares Multi-Chain Tokenized Securities Platform
description: The Korean brokerage is preparing money market funds for domestic and overseas markets while examining how financial institutions can operate settlement systems around the clock.
why_it_matters: Supporting multiple networks may reduce dependence on a single infrastructure provider, but coordination between brokerages remains an operational hurdle for continuous settlement.
keyTakeaways: KB Securities is designing infrastructure to accommodate multiple blockchain networks.
A money market fund is its planned initial tokenized product.
Continuous settlement across brokerages remains a challenge.
Park identified AI as important for migrating legacy processes into smart contracts.
body:
KB Securities outlined its approach to tokenized securities at an Ethereum Korea policy seminar in Seoul on November 23, according to separate reports by EDAILY and Byline Network. Park Jae-man, who leads the brokerage's AI and digital division, said the company is designing infrastructure that can accommodate different blockchain environments rather than relying on one network.

EDAILY reported that the brokerage has selected a money market fund as its initial tokenized product and is preparing offerings for domestic and international markets. Park also identified continuous settlement as an industry challenge. Byline Network reported that he emphasized the difficulty of coordinating round-the-clock systems across multiple securities firms and described artificial intelligence as important for migrating existing business logic into smart contracts. The remarks describe preparations and operational goals, not a completed commercial platform launch.

facts.claim: Park spoke at an Ethereum Korea policy seminar in Seoul on November 23.
KB Securities selected a money market fund as its initial tokenized security product.
The brokerage is designing architecture to accommodate different blockchain infrastructures.
Park identified shared round-the-clock operation across securities firms as an industry challenge.
Park described AI as essential to migrating existing securities systems to blockchain workflows.
facts.anchor: AI is not optional but mandatory
